title: Find All Numbers Disappeared in an Array
spaceBreakdown:
- result vector: up to n entries → not counted (returned output)
- no other containers, no recursion → O(1) auxiliary
- not counted: input array (modified in place)
approach: Since every value is in [1, n] and indices run [0, n−1], each value v naturally maps to slot v−1. We use the sign of each slot as a presence flag: for every value v, negate nums[v−1] (if not already negative). After one pass, any slot still positive means its index+1 was never seen. A second pass collects those indices+1. This is O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space because we reuse the input array.
hints:
Every value lies in [1, n] and the array has exactly n slots indexed 0…n−1. What could each value tell you about one specific slot in the array itself?
The constraints guarantee 1 ≤ nums[i] ≤ n where n is the array length.

In-place sign marking: for each value v, negate the element at index v−1 to record that v was seen.
For nums = [4,3,2,7,8,2,3,1], value 4 → negate index 3, giving [4,3,2,−7,8,2,3,1].

**Smallest input** - n = 1, the only valid value is 1
`Input: nums = [1]` → `Expected: []`
⚠️ Bug: using `nums[i]` as the index directly (no `-1`) → accesses index 1, out of bounds

**All duplicates** - same value repeated, marking collides on one slot
`Input: nums = [2,2]` → `Expected: [1]`
⚠️ Bug: negating `nums[idx]` unconditionally without checking `> 0` → second visit restores it to positive, returns `[1,2]`

**Already complete** - every number 1..n appears exactly once
`Input: nums = [1,2,3,4]` → `Expected: []`
⚠️ Bug: collecting indices where `nums[i] < 0` (inverted sign check) → returns `[1,2,3,4]`

**Largest value marks last slot** - value n must reach index n−1
`Input: nums = [4,3,2,1]` → `Expected: []`
⚠️ Bug: using `nums[i] - 1` but with `nums[i]` already negated and no `abs` → uses negative index, out of bounds

followUps.q: What if the input array is read-only and cannot be modified?
followUps.a: Allocate a boolean/bitset of size n and apply the same marking idea externally - set bit v−1 for each value v, then collect indices whose bit is still 0. Time stays O(n); auxiliary space becomes O(n).

followUps.q: What if values can range over [1, k] with k much larger than n?
followUps.a: The index-as-slot trick breaks because values exceed the array bounds. Store seen values in a hash set, then scan 1..k collecting missing ones. Time O(n + k), space O(n).

followUps.q: What if the array arrives as a stream too large to hold in memory at once?
followUps.a: Process it in fixed-size chunks, updating an external bitset of n bits (n/8 bytes) as each chunk arrives. After the stream ends, scan the bitset for zero bits. Time O(n), space O(n/8) bytes.
